chapter: Leaving home: Fisk, Tulsa, Arkansas City
title: Riding freight trains back to Oklahoma
summary: Broke, they rode freights from Nashville to Knoxville and back, dodging railway agents who shot at them, until an old landlady fed them and sent them home.

story.theme_name: Race and segregation in the jazz life
story.community_name: Segregation on the road and the bandstand

blocks.x: So we caught a freight train and went to Knoxville.
(Laughter.)
So the guy told us, he says --
How far is that?
Knoxville is, oh, I'd say about 300 miles from there.
Had you ever caught a freight train before?
Had never caught one before. But we caught the freight and went to Knoxville.
Where did you ride on the thing? In a car or --

Well, sometimes -- you know those oil cars, you know, got the ring around them, you know? We'd stand up and ride those. Sometimes there was an open boxcar and we'd get in the boxcar if they wasn't traveling too fast. And sometimes when the special agents were bad on those trains, sometimes they'd shoot at you, you know.
Oh, they would shoot at you?

Oh, yes. So we'd get in those refrigerator cars, but we'd pull the inside lock inside and then pull the door down, so they couldn't lock us in. So we learned a lot of stuff in a hurry. We learned it fast.
(Laughter.)
Would they just shoot at you for being there?

Oh, yes. Oh, yes. Well, I'll tell you what happened. We had this to happen to us. See, after we got to Knoxville, things got tough again, so we decided there ain't nothing for us to do but go back home. So we left Knoxville, going back home, and we went into Chattanooga and

leaving Chattanooga, going through Nashville, you go through those Lookout Mountains, you know. Some people call them the Blue Mountains. And we were on this freight and the old guy put us off. Okay, put us off, so the next time we caught a car with a lot of junk in it, a lot of iron and stuff, iron ore and stuff. So we figured we'd hide down between there where they couldn't see us. So open the boxcar, you know, and that guy come through there and found us again --
The same guy?

Same guy. See, what we did, we let part of the train go by and then caught it again. So he told us, "I told you. Now next time, I'm going to shoot you." But we was determined to make it, so we let about eight or ten, 15 cars go by, and we got on it again.
(Laughter.)

We got on it again. We got in this refrigerator car, had no idea -- we knew we had it beat, you know, because when he came along that refrigerator car, he pulled the door open, he pulled it open. He says, "Here you are again." And he shot, you know. I imagine he probably shot in the air. I don't know what he shot, because he didn't hit us. But we jumped up out of there and we jumped -- we got out. So by that time, the end of the freight is gone. So we said, "Here we are." We walked about a mile. So we finally said, "There's no need to walk. We might as well just stop here

and maybe take us a nap and wait for the next freight to come by." So that's what we did. We waited until the next freight came by. So the next freight came by. Sometimes, you know, my buddy used to be a little bit slow about catching those freights, but I told him, I said, "Now look, this time don't be slow, because I don't want to have to leave you out here in these mountains. We both got to get it. You get it and I'm going to get it."
So we got it.
Did he get it ahead of you or something or did you each pick a car?

We'd each pick one, you know. There's a certain way that you catch that freight because you don't want to catch it on the -- you catch it on the front end that's coming to you on the -- I believe it's the right side, front end, not the lower end, because that will whip you all around, you know what I mean. You catch that front end, you can brace yourself.

So that's what we did. So we came on into Nashville. So we was ashamed to go out there to see Mrs. Grimes. But we went by the old lady's where we had stayed, because she told us -- she said, "The only thing I can do for you, fellas, I can fix you some bacon and eggs and send you on your way." So she did. She fixed bacon and eggs and we went on and rode all the way back to Oklahoma on the freight. And so quite
